titel: What's Going On With Chase Ink Approvals in 2026

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Analyzing actual Chase Ink approval data, LLC preferences, and card strategy for 2026.
kurzfassung: This episode examines current data points on Chase Ink credit card approvals and recent changes to application terms. It highlights a distinct preference by Chase for registered LLCs and corporations over sole proprietors. Additionally, the episode covers emerging rules around Chase Sapphire card bonuses and long-term application strategies.
stichpunkte: Chase added new terms in November 2025 restricting welcome bonuses for no-fee Ink cards if you have previously held certain business cards.
Data indicates that Chase strongly favors registered LLCs and corporations over sole proprietors for business card approvals.
Sole proprietors holding three or more Chase business cards face an approval rate of approximately 10% for additional business cards.
Applicants with an LLC or corporation are successfully getting approved for repeat Ink card bonuses despite previous card ownership.
Having an EIN alone does not help sole proprietors bypass the strict approval hurdles for no-fee Ink cards.
Filing costs to establish an LLC vary significantly by state, ranging from around $50 to over $700.
Data on Chase Sapphire cards suggests that waiting eight years or more since previously holding the card yields favorable approval odds.
Targeted pre-approved offers inside Chase accounts should be viewed with caution, as some users receiving these offers still face denial.

clips.hook: New Chase Ink terms introduced in late 2025
clips.text: In late 2025, Chase updated application terms on the Chase Ink Business Cash and Chase Ink Business Unlimited cards, linking past ownership of any no-fee business card to potential bonus restrictions.

clips.hook: Approval rates drop to 10% for sole proprietors
clips.text: Applicants operating as sole proprietors with three or more existing Chase business cards face an approval rate of only 10% when applying for another business card.

clips.hook: Why having an EIN isn't enough
clips.text: Merely obtaining an Employer Identification Number does not solve approval issues for sole proprietors, as Chase specifically evaluates the underlying business structure.

clips.hook: Filing an LLC fee and getting approved
clips.text: After paying a filing fee of one hundred dollars to register an LLC in Georgia, a local applicant quickly gained approval for a previously restricted Ink card.

clips.hook: Pre-approved offers that lead to denials
clips.text: Account dashboard messages claiming an applicant is already approved for a card can still result in a final denial upon submission.
